points: This carryover audit supplements only G2 and G3; G0/G4/G5/G1 are inherited from the captured record.

A real Chrome session read both complete US-English pages without CAPTCHA. The first page contains the 24-hour-old GitHub changelog, GitHub's exact organization dashboard guide, product docs, Count's independent trend-analysis product, roadmap issues, an earlier targeting update and tool roundups; page two continues with GitHub Code Quality, generic quality tooling and marketplace options.

G2=pass: the SERP is mixed across documentation, roadmap issues, product pages, integration tooling and generic analysis. It is not a media/wiki/homepage takeover and still allows task-focused pages to compete.

GitHub Docs is a full native completion: it shows prerequisites, navigation to Security and quality > Insights > Code quality, Health and Trends tabs, filters, repository scoring and how open findings change over selected periods.

Count is a second independent free-start completion: its live page connects GitHub data, automatically tracks cross-repository code-quality trends, answers six-month and declining-quality questions, and exposes transparent SQL/Python analysis with a no-card free start.

G3=veto: at least two stable independent task completions already exist—GitHub's native organization dashboard and Count's GitHub-data trend analysis. Changelog and roadmap pages add further formation/availability coverage but are not needed for the veto.
